opening: I am writing to apply for the Forward Deployed Engineer role at Otherworldly. What drew me to the posting is that the job is defined by the boundary itself: sitting with the booking and artist-care teams, watching how the work actually happens, and turning the most manual parts of their day into deployed software. An AI-native talent management and booking company running a real roster, a database of 250,000+ bookers and algorithmic pitching systems is exactly the kind of environment where LLM orchestration, rapid prototyping and complex API integration stop being abstractions and start being the product.
role_specific: My daily engineering workflow revolves around the exact requirements outlined in your role: I utilize prompt chaining, RAG architectures, and advanced workflow orchestration tools (such as n8n) to connect external APIs with foundational models like OpenAI and Anthropic's Claude, working in Python and TypeScript. Integrating LLMs into real products through API calls, prompt design and structured outputs is what my last three years have consisted of, and the strong-plus you list, building internal tools, workflow automation and CRM and outbound systems, is a fair description of most of what I have shipped. At FlowSpace the GTM automations ran through the CRM; the freelance work for UltraStrategy and Get2Germany was internal tooling and workflow automation for people who had been doing that work by hand. I am comfortable taking a problem end to end and shipping in days rather than sprints.
closing: I would welcome the chance to talk through how I would approach the first workflow you would want removed from someone's day.
